filename: Multi-Fidelity Climate Model Parameterization for Better Generalization and Extrapolation.pdf
title: Multi-fidelity climate model parameterization for better generalization and extrapolation
parameterization_target: Subgrid-scale convective tendencies of temperature (heat tendency) and specific humidity (moisture tendency)
testbed_rationale: Provides a clear benchmark testbed for multi-fidelity scientific machine learning in climate parameterization, combining abundant low-fidelity (CAM5) simulations with scarce high-fidelity (SPCAM5) simulations to test out-of-distribution extrapolation in warmer climate regimes (+4K).
pain_points: Machine-learning parameterizations fail to extrapolate or generalize to unseen climate regimes (out-of-distribution data such as +4K warming).
High-fidelity storm-resolving simulations (e.g., SPCAM5) are computationally prohibitive to run for long multi-year durations, resulting in scarce high-fidelity training data.
Higher stochasticity and variability of humidity and convection compared to temperature make moisture tendency difficult to predict.
Standard Bayesian deep learning methods (MCMC, dropout, variational inference, standard deep ensembles) suffer from computational intractability or severe posterior variance underestimation.
Distribution shift across different warming regimes creates normalization challenges for multi-fidelity deep neural networks.
extraction_notes: The paper focuses entirely on offline parameterization and uncertainty quantification; online coupling within an Earth System Model is highlighted as future work.
